$comment: SPEC §33.1 / §6.4 / §25.4 — the vocabulary of a voice note. Added in M9 for the reason every other set in this package was added: the two languages already held different versions of it. `services/api`'s message store wrote `transcript_status: "not_applicable"` and `playback_policy: "text_only"`; `apps/web`'s VoiceNoteBubble declared `TranscriptStatus = "ready" | "pending" | "failed" | "none"`. Neither had ever crossed the wire, so nothing failed — the same invisibility that hid the confidence states, the presence states and the memory types until the first screen rendered one. M9's bubble is that first screen, so the set lands here before it does.

transcript_status.$comment: §6.4's `messages.transcript_status`, one of §33.1's six explicit fields. `not_applicable` is a TYPED message — the field is required on every message row, so text needs a member that says 'this was never spoken' rather than a null that reads as 'transcription is still coming'. §28.3's failure row is `failed`: 'transcribe-fail → send as text? original audio preserved' — the audio survives a failed transcript, which is why this is a status and not a delete trigger.

members.note: a typed message; nothing was spoken
audio received, STT not finished (§28.3: transcript <2s post-release)
§28.3 — STT failed; the ORIGINAL audio is preserved regardless

playback_policy.$comment: §6.4's `messages.playback_policy`, and the field §25.4's central promise rests on: 'replay plays the user's ORIGINAL recording per the §33.1 storage policy, never a TTS reconstruction'. That sentence is only enforceable if a bubble can tell the three cases apart, which is what this enum is for. `synthesised` is the ONLY member under which audio is a reconstruction, and §25.4 makes it illegal on a user message — a rule the store enforces structurally rather than by review.

members.note: a typed message; there is no audio and no control
§25.4/§33.1 default — replay plays the user's own recording

§33.1 — audio expired, was deleted, or was never stored (delete-after-transcription). The bubble drops playback and shows the transcript with a 'voice input' marker. This is the honest state, not a degraded one.
§25.4 — Tara's own voice-note reply, rendered from her TTS with a transcript toggle. NEVER valid on a user message: that substitution is precisely what §25.4 names as the thing not to do.

vad_state.$comment: §34.6's `vad.state` payload. In M9 this brackets a HELD recording rather than reporting server-side voice activity detection — §25.4's grammar is hold-to-record or tap-lock, so the client knows when speech starts and stops because the user's finger says so. M10's live calls add the server-VAD sense of the same member (§25.3's barge-in ducking); the members below are chosen so that addition is a widening, not a rename.

members.note: the hold began; binary frames may now follow
released or locked-then-stopped; the note is complete
§28.3's cancel-slide — discard, never transcribe, never store. A live call never sends this: nothing was held, so there is nothing to slide away from.

barge_in_reason.$comment: §34.6's `barge_in` payload (M10). §25.3 gives exactly one way to interrupt Tara — 'barge-in = just speak' — so `user_speech` is the only member that describes a user's action, and it is deliberately not spelled `user_interrupt`: the user did not press anything, which is the whole feature. The other two members exist because the client's job is identical in all three cases (drop the buffer, expect no `tts.end`) while the reason it must SAY to the user is not: an utterance cut by a provider failure is §8's degrade ladder and an utterance cut by an exhausted minute pool is §32.9's, and a client that could not tell them apart would show 'she stopped speaking' for both.

members.note: §25.3 — server-side VAD heard the user while she was speaking
§8 — synthesis died mid-utterance; the words survive as text
§32.9 — the minute pool hit zero mid-utterance

SOURCE_AUDIO_RETENTION_DAYS.$comment: §33.1 — 'the original recording is stored encrypted for 30 days BY DEFAULT'. Default, so a user setting may shorten it; the expiry job reads the per-note `source_audio_expires_at` rather than this constant, which exists so both sides can render the same promise in the same words.

MAX_NOTE_DURATION_MS.$comment: A cap, not a spec value. §34.6's frame is 16kHz mono s16le = 32 kB/s, so two minutes is ~3.8 MB — comfortably inside MongoDB's 16 MB document limit, which is where §33.1's CSFLE key class puts the bytes. The client stops recording here rather than letting a pocket-dial write a document that cannot be stored.

ENTITLEMENT_WARNING_MINUTES.$comment: §32.9 — 'warnings at 5 and 2 minutes (in-locale, in Tara's voice, once each)'. Descending, because that is the order they fire in and a reader should not have to work it out. Both sides need the same two numbers: the server decides when to send `entitlement.warning`, the client decides when the §25.3 plan chip stops saying 'unlimited' and starts counting, and a chip that appeared at a different number from the warning would be two implementations of one promise.

HOLDING_PHRASE_AFTER_MS.$comment: §25.3 — the thinking state is 'a brief shimmer on the waveform — max 1.8s before she speaks a holding phrase'. A ceiling on silence, not a delay to wait out: if §9 answers in 400ms she answers in 400ms. It lives here because the server decides to speak the phrase and the client decides how long to shimmer, and those two have to be the same 1.8 seconds or the shimmer either ends before she speaks or outlasts her.
